preconditions.description: T is a positive integer representing the number of test cases, with T ≤ 50.

preconditions.expression: all(N.is_integer() and 4 <= N <= 64 for N in [int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and line.split()[0].isdigit()])
preconditions.description: Each test case starts with an integer N where 4 ≤ N ≤ 64.

preconditions.expression: all(len(matrix) == N and all(len(row) == N and all(1 <= int(val) <= N*N for val in row) for row in matrix) for matrix in [[list(map(int, line.split())) for line in lines[1:N+1]] for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+N+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)]])
preconditions.description: Each test case contains an N×N matrix where each cell value is an integer between 1 and N² inclusive.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly T lines, one for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all(output_line.is_integer() and output_line >= 0 for output_line in [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()])
postconditions.description: Each output line is a non-negative integer representing the minimal number of operations.

postconditions.expression: all(min_operations >= 0 for min_operations in [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()])
postconditions.description: The minimal number of operations is always non-negative.

postconditions.expression: all(operations == 0 or (operations > 0 and is_possible_to_sort(matrix, operations)) for matrix, operations in zip([[[int(val) for val in line.split()] for line in lines[1:N+1]] for lines in [stdin.splitlines()[i:i+N+1] for i in range(1, len(stdin.splitlines()), N+1)]], [int(line) for line in stdout.splitlines()]))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output is the smallest number of operations such that the matrix can be sorted using exactly that many operations. The helper `is_possible_to_sort(matrix, k)` checks if the matrix can be sorted in at most k operations.
